As of 325 PM EDT Sunday..

KEY MESSAGE 1...Chance for showers and
storms returns today and Monday as a slow-moving front moves 
in.

Latest wx analysis shows a slow moving cold front across the Ohio 
River Valley slowly approaching the area today and Monday. With
the front approaching, there is a chance of showers/storms both
days. This afternoon/evening, the best chance for scattered 
showers/storms will be in the north/northwest portions of the 
area. An isolated strong to severe storm with damaging wind 
gusts in the piedmont cannot be ruled out, as SPC maintains a 
Marginal Risk of severe weather across this area today. With the
approaching front being rather weak and not having enough 
strength to cross the local area, storms will likely struggle to
become strong from lack of forcing. Some shower activity could 
linger into the overnight hours.

Monday, the slow moving front will continue to push further south, 
potentially taking all day to reach the NC border, and then pushing 
back north overnight. This will create quite a gradient in 
temperatures for Monday. For those north of the front, generally 
Richmond and north, highs will top out in the upper 70s to lower 
80s. South of the front, mid to upper 80s will once again make their 
presence known. Our far southern NC localities could even approach 
90 degrees. If the front does change its timing at all, this will 
affect the temperature forecast. The front will once again bring 
another chance of showers and storms, with the best chance south of 
the front with the higher amounts of instability. Showers and storms 
may be able to develop in the southern half of the area Monday 
afternoon with the front and building back towards the northern 
half. SPC has maintained a Marginal Risk of severe weather west of I-
95, with the main threat being damaging wind gusts. WPC 
continues with a Marginal Risk of excessive flooding for areas 
generally west of I-95 as well. 


KEY MESSAGE 2...Persistent onshore flow and a potentially 
strengthening coastal low will create a wetter, cooler, and breezier 
forecast for most of the week.  

The forecast for the rest of the week will be highly dependent on 
the location and strength of a developing low pressure off the 
coast. With the large high pressure parked to our north, we will be 
entering a prolonged period of onshore flow. A Cold Air Damming 
wedge set up looks likely for us Tuesday into Wednesday, though it 
isn't quite as strong as what models were portraying the last few 
days. With the wedge, forecast highs vary greatly across the area 
with highs on Tuesday in the lower 70s (locally upper 60s) in the 
piedmont and MD Eastern Shore and lower to mid 80s across SE VA/NE 
NC. Wednesday's highs are cooler with temperatures in the lower 60s 
across the piedmont to mid 70s across SE VA/NE NC. Will note that 
the NAM, which typically is the most aggressive (but can have the 
right idea with wedge set ups) has highs in the mid 50s in the 
piedmont and lower 70s along the coast on Wednesday. 

Along with the cooler temperatures, breezy winds and wet conditions 
are expected through the end of the week. Winds will begin to 
increase on Tuesday as well, with coastal areas seeing gusty 
conditions by the evening and potentially lasting all the way into 
at least Friday. Rain chances will persist each day next week, with 
WPC placing us in a Marginal Risk of Excessive Rainfall each day. 
The previous Slight Risk on Tuesday has been removed. Guidance does 
keep trying to develop localized areas of significant rainfall 
totals off and on through the period, so keep in mind that some 
instances of flash flooding may be possible as those rain chances 
remain. Some guidance is even showing a secondary surface low 
developing off our coast later in the week, which would prolong the 
period of impactful weather even longer. Regardless, this coastal 
low will bring impactful weather to our area for an extended period 
of time. Model differences and timing limitations are still creating 
some uncertainty in the details, so please stay tuned to the latest 
forecast as we work out the details.  


KEY MESSAGE 3...Widespread minor to moderate tidal flooding 
(inundation of 1-2 feet AGL in vulnerable areas) is likely by the 
middle of the week due to strong northeast winds, with localized 
major tidal flooding possible.

least Thursday, which will cause water levels to rise across much of 
the area (especially along the bay, tidal rivers, and Atlantic 
coast). No tidal flooding is expected through Tuesday. A significant
